title: Identity and composition laws for explicitly constructed outgoing-arrow product transitions
statement: Let I be a preordered set, D : Iᵒᵖ → Sch a diagram, and F_i abelian sheaves on the small etale sites of D_i. Write J_k = Injective.under(F_k) and FI_i = product over outgoing h : i → k of (D(h.op))_* J_k. Define psi_f : (D(f.op))^* FI_i → FI_j by the product universal property: its component at g : j → k is the inverse adjoint transpose, along D(f.op), of the projection to the factor indexed by f≫g followed by the inverse of the direct-image composition comparison lowerStarComp(D(g.op), D(f.op), D((f≫g).op), D.map_comp). Then psi_id is the canonical inverse-image identity comparison transported along D.map_id, and psi_(f≫g) = upperStarComp(D(g.op), D(f.op), D((f≫g).op), D.map_comp) followed by (D(g.op))^*(psi_f) and psi_g. No coefficient transitions, embedding, directedness or nonemptiness are assumed.

proof.text: Define each psi_f by the explicit Pi.lift and inverse homEquiv in etaleCoefficientProductTransition. Every outgoing-arrow index set is small; all products exist in the larger-universe abelian sheaf category. These maps are actual constructions and are not chosen from the existence of a compatible system.

For the identity law, project to g : i → k. The index id≫g equals g. Transport D(id.op) to the identity using D.map_id. The right unit law lowerStarComp_id_right says that the inverse composition comparison at J_k is lowerStarId.inv at (D(g.op))_* J_k. Transpose the proposed identity component. By adjunction naturality and upperStarId_hom_app_unit_app its transpose is lowerStarId.inv at FI_i followed by the identity direct image of the g projection. Naturality of lowerStarId.inv identifies this with the g projection followed by lowerStarId.inv at (D(g.op))_* J_k. Injectivity of homEquiv proves the component equation and Pi.hom_ext proves the identity law.

For composition f : i → j, g : j → k, project to h : k → l, and apply the adjunction homEquiv for D((f≫g).op). Compose both transposes with the inverse lowerStarComp for g,f. The mate/unit equation upperStarComp_hom_app_unit_app changes the transpose of the composed inverse-image maps into the composite of the individual transposes. Naturality of homEquiv and the two Pi.lift projection equations reduce the two sides to the projection indexed by (f≫g)≫h followed, respectively, by the two inverse direct-image comparisons for three morphisms. Associativity of indices follows from Category.assoc; associativity of the comparisons follows from lowerStarComp_assoc′, with all diagram composites named and D.map_comp providing the transport equalities. The inverse associativity equation identifies these two maps. Cancel the isomorphism and use injectivity of homEquiv and Pi.hom_ext.

lean.statement:
theorem etale_coefficient_product_transition_laws
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    (F : ∀ i : I, Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    (∀ i : I, etaleCoefficientProductTransition D F (𝟙 i) =
      (eqToIso (congrArg (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (D.map_id (op i)))).hom.app
        (etaleCoefficientInjectiveTarget D F i) ≫
      (upperStarId AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.obj (op i))).hom.app
        (etaleCoefficientInjectiveTarget D F i)) ∧
    (∀ (i j k : I) (f : i ⟶ j) (g : j ⟶ k),
      etaleCoefficientProductTransition D F (f ≫ g) =
        (upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.map g.op) (D.map f.op)
          (D.map (f ≫ g).op) (D.map_comp g.op f.op)).hom.app
            (etaleCoefficientInjectiveTarget D F i) ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.map g.op)).map
          (etaleCoefficientProductTransition D F f) ≫ etaleCoefficientProductTransition D F g)
